sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: HiBiT-FZD6 was used in kinetic WNT-3A binding experiments in living HEK293A cells, confirming surface display. FZD6 did not transduce WNT-3A-induced β-catenin/TOPFlash signaling, consistent with known FZD6 biology (non-canonical Wnt receptor), not a tag-induced defect. No canonical signaling assay was passed, but surface display was confirmed by the binding assay itself.
sites.rationale: The ledger (L1) explicitly reports an N-terminal HiBiT tag on full-length FZD6 used in live-cell binding assays, confirming surface display. The signal peptide ends at residue 18 (G) and the mature extracellular domain begins at residue 19 (H), making insert_after_residue=18 the sole possible extracellular N-terminal junction; this is computed from the authoritative topology landmarks, not chosen. The position is topology_derived because the paper names 'N-terminal' but no residue number. Multiple independent constructs (Nluc-FZD6, SNAP-FZD6, N-terminal mCherry) from three separate publications converge on this same junction, providing strong convergent support. Full-length human FZD6 carrying an N-terminal HiBiT tag was generated and expressed in HEK293A cells for NanoBiT/BRET kinetic binding assays (PMC8205236). The construct sequence was verified and used in live-cell binding experiments. The same N-terminal position is independently supported by Nluc-FZD6 (PMC12605013, L3/L5) and SNAP-FZD6 (PMC12605013, L4) constructs, and by the N-terminal mCherry in pmCherry-FZD6-mCherry (PMC7324525, L6). The paper states 'N-terminal HiBiT tag' but names no residue number; the signal peptide spans 1–18 (MATURE_N-TERMINUS = 19), so the only extracellular N-terminal junction is after residue 18 (G) and before residue 19 (H).

sources.claim: In order to establish a nanoluciferase complementation-dependent NanoBiT/BRET binding assay format to study all human FZD paralogues, we generated constructs for all 10 receptors carrying an N-terminal HiBiT tag ( Figure S1A,B ).

literature_notes: Six ledger lines were evaluated. L1–L5 all support the same N-terminal extracellular junction (after signal peptide cleavage at residue 18); they differ only in tag identity (HiBiT, Nluc, SNAP) and publication, not in position, so they constitute one site. L6 (pmCherry-FZD6-mCherry) provides both an N-terminal mCherry (same extracellular site) and a C-terminal mCherry; the C-terminus falls within IC4 (residues 495–706, intracellular) and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports a tag insertion in any of the short extracellular loops (EC2: 255–283, EC3: 349–368, EC4: 438–472), so no internal loop sites are proposed. The ΔCRD-FZD6 construct (L4, starting from D156) is a truncated ectodomain-deleted construct used as a cloning template, not a validated internal insertion site, and is not promoted to a site.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal mCherry in pmCherry-FZD6-mCherry; residue 706 (T) lies within IC4 (495–706), the long intracellular C-terminal tail, so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface tag site.
